record.original_question: Regression in the $\ell_p$ norm: Consider the $ell_p$ linear regression problem minimize_x R^d |Ax - b |_ell_p for a matrix (A R^n x d ) and a vector (b R^n ). For a sketching matrix (Omega R^n x k ), the sketch-and-solve solution is [~ x argmin_x R^d |(Omega^ -> p Ax)-(Omega^ -> p b) |_ell_p. ] Formulate a generalization of the OSI property to the $ell_p$ regression problem which ensures that this procedure succeeds to constant-factor accuracy [ |A ~ x - b |_ell_p <= const* _x R^d |Ax - b |_ell_p. ]

evidence.quote: Consider the $\ell_p$ linear regression problem % \begin{equation*} \operatorname{minimize}_{x \in\mathbb{R}^d} \|Ax - b\|_{\ell_p} \end{equation*} % for a matrix \(A \in \mathbb R^{n \times d}\) and a vector \(b\in\mathbb R^{n}\). For a sketching matrix \(\Omega \in \mathbb R^{n \times k}\), the sketch-and-solve solution is \[\tilde x \in \operatorname{argmin}_{x \in\mathbb{R}^d} \|(\Omega^\top Ax)-(\Omega^\top b)\|_{\ell_p}.\] Formulate a generalization of the OSI property to the $\ell_p$ regression problem which ensures that this procedure succeeds to constant-factor accuracy %(i.e., without an assumption on the \(\ell_p\) norm dilation) \[ \|A \tilde x - b \|_{\ell_p} \leq \mathrm{const}\cdot \min_{x \in \mathbb R^d}\|Ax - b\|_{\ell_p}. \] % Devise a generalization of the OSI condition which provides guarantees for sketched linear regression in the \(\ell_p\) norm. % Low-rank approximation in some matrix \(\ell_p\) norm?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $1 \le p < \infty$. Consider the $\ell_p$ linear regression problem
$$\min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} \|Ax - b\|_{\ell_p},$$
where $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}$ and $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Given a (possibly random) sketching matrix $\Omega \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$, the sketch-and-solve estimator is
$$\tilde x \in \operatorname{argmin}_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} \|\Omega^{\top} A x - \Omega^{\top} b\|_{\ell_p}.$$

Recall that, in the $\ell_2$ setting, the Oblivious Subspace Inequality / Embedding (OSI) property of $\Omega$ with respect to a subspace $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ asserts that, with high probability over $\Omega$, the map $v \mapsto \Omega^\top v$ preserves $\ell_2$ norms on $V$ up to constant multiplicative distortion, which suffices to guarantee that the sketch-and-solve solution to $\ell_2$ regression achieves
$$\|A\tilde x - b\|_{\ell_2} \le C \min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d}\|Ax - b\|_{\ell_2}$$
for an absolute constant $C$.

Task: Formulate an analogous "$\ell_p$-OSI" condition on the sketching matrix $\Omega \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ (depending only on $\Omega$ and possibly on the column span of $A$ and the residual direction, but not on any a priori bound on the $\ell_p$ norm dilation of $\Omega$) such that, whenever $\Omega$ satisfies this condition, the sketch-and-solve estimator $\tilde x$ above satisfies
$$\|A\tilde x - b\|_{\ell_p} \le C_p \cdot \min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d}\|Ax - b\|_{\ell_p}$$
for a constant $C_p$ depending only on $p$. Prove that the proposed condition implies this constant-factor approximation guarantee.
artifact.category_tag: Sketching and randomized numerical linear algebra
artifact.status_search_result: The question asks for a formulation of a generalized OSI-type condition guaranteeing constant-factor sketch-and-solve accuracy for $\ell_p$ regression. While there is a substantial literature on $\ell_p$-subspace embeddings and Lewis-weight sampling (e.g., Sohler–Woodruff, Cohen–Peng, Wang–Woodruff) that gives constant-factor guarantees for $\ell_p$ regression, no single canonical "$\ell_p$-OSI" condition aligned with the framing of this open prompt has been verified. The status as a precise formulation problem is unknown.
